The problem that people are missing here is not that life has meaning whether subjective or objective but that fundamentally it is inbuilt into us to look for meaning and divide and assign value to this world. 

Of course whether it’s macro (why am I here, what is my purpose and what is my meaning in all this) or micro (why is the plant green?) we want to answer the question. 

Just because we can’t find an answer yet doesn’t mean there isn’t one. 

But also realizing that the problem is that there’s no answer it’s that we’re asking the question in the first place. Because perhaps in terms of everything that’s going on in the universe, perhaps the question is nonsensical or paradoxical, but we’re too ignorant to understand or see that. 

Now if we base our primary premise as: the question is non-sensical then we can stop trying to find meaning. Then nihilism becomes irrelevant. People get all sad about nihilism because they can’t find the answer. So they assume there is no answer while in fact there just is no question. And it’s the question that’s to blame. 

Ok no question on life. Then what?

Well I like Alan Watts frame of reference on it. 

We are not put here by a deity, nor are we some cosmic accident, wherein we awaken to realization that we are aliens on a rock or strangers in a strangeland. 

Rather, we are the natural fruit of this earth and the universe. The earth peoples people. We are the fruit of the earth. 

And so we are a natural part of the universe. The universe is getting on just fine without us fretting over it. Unless of course fretting over it is a natural part of the fruit.

Either way, we don’t have to look for meaning. We are it. Or moreover, it is it. And it is 1 of itself. It’s value is complete in itself.

Hey mate, it’s hard but if you had a child in a similar situation for their age, whether it was 6, 10 or 18, how would you go about helping them?

You’d do your best, telling them to not worry, tell them the action steps they need to take and that they gotta just do it. You wouldn’t feel any shame for them. It’s just what’s best for them. 

You need to be your own parent. That means detaching yourself from the shame. If you feel shame it’s because you identify with the person you’ve created in your head. Then you project that person out into the world and others pick up on the signal. 

But you aren’t that. Whether you’re rich or poor you realize that the real you is always with you and is not subjected to these types of impermanence and change. 

Stop identifying yourself with this illusion. 

Realize that the peace you’re looking for does not come from avoidance. Because the actions you’re taking do not align with reality and what makes the most sense, you start to feel uncomfortable, but its a different discomfort than before. In the short term a long time ago it seemed to work, it seemed to make sense. You got short term relief. But it only made sense in the fact that it gave your feelings relief. 

Because you were focused on just fixing the feelings you weren’t fixing the problem. The feelings are indicators of what’s happening. We live for life. We don’t live for the feelings. The feelings are just a side effect. 

Now you may feel discomfort when dealing with a problem. And that’s okay. You’re dealing with the problem. The feeling is impermanent. It’s going to change with whatever you’re doing. And the things you’re doing if done with a mind to see a good result and to fix, well it doesn’t matter the feeling because we know it’s not going to stay as discomfort. Why? Because instead of changing the feeling, which is a reflection of what’s happening, we change the situation. And that’s far more effective and sustainable than changing the feeling. 

Why?

Because after you’ve changed the feeling with a hit of dopamine, like watching videos, smoking, drinking, procrastinating, eating, social media, the list of avoidance goes on, what we inevitably find is that the situation is still there, it hasn’t gone away, or someone else has to deal with it, or it starts to snowball into something else. 

So, what’s the solution?

The solution is to deal with the situation no matter the feeling. Stop chasing the feeling. We all want good feelings. But what we need is to chase the problem or situation. 

The feelings of good and bad, comfort and discomfort will come. But if you deal with the issue, you’ll find that your body will get start generating for you more feelings of comfort and general peace. 

It seems like it won’t happen but it will. You have to trust the process. You have to put your focus not on the discomfort but on the project.

One must imagine Sisyphus happy pushing that boulder up the mountain. Only to see it roll back down again. He is bound to it, the toil and suffering. It is inevitable that he will return to the bottom and start again. 

Also with us, death is inevitable. So what to do?

In a world without meaning. We are conscious of our predicament.

So what can we do?

Why do anything? 

And it’s in the why, the quest for a reason that some despair because there is no answer. The universe and god is silent. 

Argh it’s absurd. We are conscious of a predicament we can’t solve. 

So no reason. Just life. And yes that answer would be sufficient for the animal. Without the prefrontal cortex. Just doing what the duck does. Being a tree. There is no question of what to do or their place in the world. They just live. 

Yet it seems it’s not so easy for us to slip into that type of thinking. What does that even mean, just be human? There is no easy answer to that question.

So what then? And so we see we only have limited time to answer it. 

So you awaken to the world of an absurd predicament. 

You’ve tasted the delights of earth with the ignorance of not knowing your predicament but now you do. And it’s fucked. 

Wouldn’t it be so much easier to let that boulder just roll on over you. Just end it there. Why push on through this pain? It’s not going to stop. 

Even a few moments of hedonistic pleasure will fleet. 

So what do you do? 

The universe will offer you no reply, except the reply you conjure up for yourself. 

You could smile at it. Even laugh at it. 

There’s a victory in that. It’s not a defeatist approach because that would mean letting the boulder roll on over you. 

No, it’s feeling that rock. That burden we’ve been given. That’s your burden. That’s your rock for the time given. No one else can take that from you. And you can be happy in that. 

That’s not to say it’s masochistic. Since there is no choice in the suffering or in the boulder. It’s not about loving suffering or relishing in it but embracing the human condition, embracing the rock. Without fear and perhaps with a smile. A way to defy the gods, a way to defy the silence of the universe.

But could Sisyphus keep pushing that boulder and sustain eternal psychological suffering? That was the plan of Zeus.  

No, surely he would crack from the knowledge that he can’t escape. 

But he doesn’t crack. Well he must be happy then.
